message.subject: This week: five things worth reading

signals.title: Reply-To points at a different organisation
signals.explanation: A reply would be delivered to no-reply@mailprovider.example at mailprovider.example, not to newsletter.example. Redirecting replies is how a conversation is moved somewhere the real sender cannot see it. This message carries bulk-mail headers (List-Id, List-Unsubscribe, Precedence), where this pattern is routine, so the finding is weighted down rather than removed.
signals.advice: Check where a reply would actually go before responding.

signals.title: Message-ID domain does not match the sender
signals.explanation: The Message-ID was generated at mailprovider.example while the message claims to be from newsletter.example. This is normal for mail sent through a service provider, so it only matters alongside the other findings here. This message carries bulk-mail headers (List-Id, List-Unsubscribe, Precedence), where this pattern is routine, so the finding is weighted down rather than removed.
signals.advice: Corroborating evidence only. Read it together with the sender findings.

signals.title: Return-Path does not match the sender
signals.explanation: Bounces for this message go to mailprovider.example, but the reader sees newsletter.example as the sender. Legitimate providers do this too, so weigh it together with the authentication and identity findings. This message carries bulk-mail headers (List-Id, List-Unsubscribe, Precedence), where this pattern is routine, so the finding is weighted down rather than removed.
signals.advice: Check whether the envelope sender is an expected mail provider for this brand.
